newsitem.title: FRANCE: US says grain export subsidies depend on EU, prices.
newsitem.headline: US says grain export subsidies depend on EU, prices.

text.p: Any decision by the United States to use export subsidies on its grain sales will depend primarily on future European Union export policy and on world price levels, a top U.S. Department of Agriciulture official said on Tuesday.

"What we will do with EEP (Export Enhancement Programme) will be determined to a large extent by what the EU does with its subsidy programme," Robert Riemenschneide, director of the grain and seed division of the USDA, told a grain conference.
Riemenschneider said that while the USDA would carefully monitor EU export policy, it would also closely watch other main grain producers such as Canada.

He added that although it was too early to predict price levels for the new 1997-98 season, these levels would also determine any decision by the U.S. to use subsidies on its exports of grain, primarily wheat.

Commenting on prospects for world wheat trade beyond the year 2000, he said the USDA expected trade to rise to 120 million tonnes by 2005 from a current 90 million. The U.S. share of world wheat trade might increase to 34 percent by 2005 from a current share of 28 percent.

Commenting on prospects for the U.S. wheat crop, which has been hit by frost, Riemenschneider said that "what was looking like an excellent crop will not be as good as expected". He provided no further details.
